## Overview

This tutorial scrapes data about Arctic Council documents. Scraping gives us access to data that is not provided through an API.

The scraping chunks below are shown but not run (`eval: false`), because they hit a live website with a 10 second crawl delay and the site may have changed. The results come from the saved `scrape.rds` and `collected_meta_result.rds` files in this repository, so the rest of the document runs offline.

## Getting ready

Load tidyverse, rvest and polite. Install any you do not already have. Alternatively, `pacman::p_load(tidyverse, rvest, polite)` loads and installs them in one step.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup-polite
#| eval: false
library(polite)
```

```{r}
#| label: main-url
main_url <- "https://oaarchive.arctic-council.org/"
```

Selector Gadget makes it easy to identify the CSS selector you want to use. Visit <https://selectorgadget.com/> and either drag the bookmarklet to your browser's toolbar or install the Chrome extension. The browser's developer tools work too.

Check whether the site permits scraping and whether it sets a crawl delay:

```{r}
#| label: bow
#| eval: false
bow <- bow(main_url)
bow
```

The site allows scraping with a 10 second delay, which a custom function can enforce.

```{r}
#| label: slow-read
slow_read <- function(url) {
  read <- read_html(url)
  Sys.sleep(10) # 10 second pause
  read
}
```

## Format search

Copy the URL from page 2 of the search results:

```{r}
#| label: copied-url
copied_url <- "https://oaarchive.arctic-council.org/discover?rpp=100&etal=0&scope=/&group_by=none&page=2&sort_by=dc.date.issued_dt&order=asc&filtertype_0=author&filter_relational_operator_0=equals&filter_0=Arctic+Council"
```

Note the parameters in the URL:

- `rpp=100` requests 100 results per page.
- `sort_by=dc.date.issued_dt` with `order=asc` sorts results by date, oldest first.
- `filter_0=Arctic+Council` limits the search to documents authored directly by the Arctic Council.

Replace the page number parameter with `{pn}` so a vector of page numbers can fill it in. There were 5 pages at 2021-01-25 02:32:40 UTC.

```{r}
#| label: q-url
pn <- 1:5

q_url <- str_glue("https://oaarchive.arctic-council.org/discover?rpp=100&etal=0&scope=/&group_by=none&page={pn}&sort_by=dc.date.issued_dt&order=asc&filtertype_0=author&filter_relational_operator_0=equals&filter_0=Arctic+Council")

# Confirm that the page numbers have been added
head(q_url)
```

Use Selector Gadget to find the CSS selector that matches each document entry.

```{r}
#| label: css-select
#| eval: false
css_select <- "#aspect_discovery_SimpleSearch_div_search-results a"
read_html(q_url[1]) %>%
  html_nodes(css = css_select) %>%
  html_attr(name = "href")
```

Each page returns 200 hrefs for 100 results, so every href appears twice. The duplicates are removed later.

## Automate scraping with purrr

```{r}
#| label: purrr-pipeline
#| eval: false
css_select <- "#aspect_discovery_SimpleSearch_div_search-results a"

p_css <- partial(html_nodes, css = css_select) # Prefill the CSS selector
p_attr <- partial(html_attr, name = "href")    # Prefill the HTML attribute

# Build a purrr custom function
p_read <- compose(p_attr,
                  p_css,
                  slow_read # custom function from earlier, with crawl delay
                  )

scrape <- map(q_url, safely(p_read)) %>% set_names(q_url)

# Save your work
saveRDS(scrape, "scrape.rds")
```

Load the saved result instead of scraping again:

```{r}
#| label: load-scrape
scrape <- readRDS("scrape.rds")
```

## Review and format document URLs

`safely()` returns a `result` and an `error` for every page. `list_transpose()` regroups the list by outcome, so all results sit together and all errors sit together. It replaces `purrr::transpose()`, which is superseded as of purrr 1.0.0. `simplify = FALSE` keeps each element as a list.

```{r}
#| label: transpose-scrape
scrape_result <- scrape %>% list_transpose(simplify = FALSE)

# Check that no page returned an error
all(map_lgl(scrape_result$error, is.null))
```

Build one tibble from all of the results with `map_dfr()`:

```{r}
#| label: scrape-res
scrape_res <- map_dfr(scrape_result$result, ~tibble(href = .x))
```

The first result's full link is <https://oaarchive.arctic-council.org/handle/11374/2047>. The scraped hrefs are only the tail of each document URL, so add a base URL to the front.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-res-mod
base_url <- "https://oaarchive.arctic-council.org"

scrape_res_mod <- scrape_res %>%
  distinct(href) %>%                     # Remove duplicate href values
  mutate(doc_url = str_c(base_url, href)) # Append base_url to the front of href

scrape_res_mod
```

## Scraping the metadata

A custom function extracts the metadata for one document and returns a tibble.

```{r}
#| label: meta-extract
meta_extract <- function(doc_url) {
  # Scrape data from page with 10 second delay
  data <- slow_read(doc_url)

  title <- html_nodes(data, css = ".first-page-header") %>%
    html_text()

  abstract <- html_nodes(data, css = ".simple-item-view-description div") %>%
    html_text()

  date <- html_nodes(data, css = ".simple-item-view-date") %>%
    html_text(trim = TRUE) %>% # Remove the white space indicating a next line
    str_sub(start = 5, end = 8) # Remove the word "Date" and extract the year

  author <- html_nodes(data, css = ".simple-item-view-authors div") %>%
    html_text()

  tib <- tibble(title, date, author, abstract, doc_url)

  tib
}
```

Test it on the first two documents, then estimate the time a full scrape would take.

```{r}
#| label: meta-test
#| eval: false
collected_meta_test <- map(scrape_res_mod$doc_url[1:2], safely(meta_extract)) %>%
  list_transpose(simplify = FALSE)

# Inspect the test scrape
collected_meta_test
```

Estimated time for scraping with the delay, in minutes:

```{r}
#| label: time-estimate
length(scrape_res_mod$doc_url) * 10 / 60
```

Begin with a sample of 5 documents:

```{r}
#| label: meta-sample
#| eval: false
collected_meta <- map(scrape_res_mod$doc_url[1:5], safely(meta_extract)) %>%
  list_transpose(simplify = FALSE) # Regroup by result and error outcomes

collected_meta_result <- collected_meta$result %>%
  bind_rows() # Combine all of the results into one tibble

collected_meta_error <- collected_meta$error %>%
  bind_rows() # Combine all of the errors into one tibble

# Save your work
saveRDS(collected_meta_result, "collected_meta_result.rds")
```

Load the previously scraped file with the full data so we can explore it:

```{r}
#| label: load-meta
collected_meta_result <- readRDS("collected_meta_result.rds")

collected_meta_result
```

## Exploring the data

How many documents were released in 1998?

```{r}
#| label: q-1998
collected_meta_result %>%
  filter(date == 1998) %>%
  count()
```

How many documents refer to Canada?

```{r}
#| label: q-canada
collected_meta_result %>%
  mutate(canada = grepl("canad", abstract, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(canada == TRUE) %>%
  count()
```

How many documents refer to the EU?

```{r}
#| label: q-eu
collected_meta_result %>%
  mutate(eu = grepl("European Union", abstract, ignore.case = FALSE)) %>%
  filter(eu == TRUE) %>%
  count()
```
